description: We are Red-Ares, an interdisciplinary team passionate about science. Our team brings together different skills across scientific research, software development, design, storytelling and more. We especially welcome people with skills in GIS /geospatial analysis, planetary science, data science and scientific research. Join Red-Ares. 🚀
summary:
As Planetary Science and Deep Space Exploration pave the way for human presence beyond Earth, transforming open-source satellite observations into actionable survival tools is essential. Addressing the critical operational need of crewed Martian missions, RED-ARES: Interplanetary Survival Guide is a Tactical Dashboard and Integrated Operations Map designed for Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) in Jezero Crater.

Developed for the Martian Map challenge, this dual-interface ecosystem bridges Earth’s Mission Control with an astronaut’s Augmented Reality (AR) helmet HUD. To overcome hazardous terrain and severe Earth-Mars communication delays, RED-ARES integrates metric-resolution HiRISE terrain models with CRISM mineralogical data. Using A* and Dijkstra algorithms enhanced with strictly positive cost-attenuation factors, it plots safe corridors — avoiding slopes >15° and soft dunes — while guiding explorers toward high-value clay and carbonate deposits. Simultaneously, it tracks real-time metabolic oxygen consumption (72–228 L/h) and triggers dynamic Point-of-No-Return alerts.

Validated with a 50-point Jezero Crater dataset, RED-ARES mitigates geological risks, optimizes life-support resources, and maximizes scientific return — ensuring humanity’s first Martian pioneers explore safely and return home
details:
Red-Ares: Interplanetary Survival Guide operates as a dual-interface ecosystem designed for Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) in Jezero Crater:

1- How It Works & System Architecture

1. Mission Control Dashboard (Earth): Scientists and mission planners analyze multi-layered orbital datasets—combining metric-resolution HiRISE & CTX Stereo DEMs (0.25–6.0 m/px) with CRISM hyperspectral mineral data—to map safe corridors and flag hazardous terrain (slopes >15° and soft aeolian dunes).

2. Astronaut AR Helmet HUD (Mars): With one click, mission plans sync to an interactive 3D Augmented Reality heads-up display. Explorers visualize 360° terrain topography, real-time areographic bearings, mineral hotspots, and life-support telemetry directly within their field of view without blocking natural vision.

2- Pathfinding Intelligence & Biomedical Modeling

To balance safety with scientific return, our routing engine implements A* and Dijkstra pathfinding algorithms governed by a strictly positive cost function:

Total_Cost = (C_terrain × μ_friction) × α_science. Instead of using negative weights that break graph admissibility, entering a 30-meter radius of high-value clay or carbonate deposits applies a positive attenuation multiplier (α_science = 0.3), safely attracting the route toward scientific targets.

Simultaneously, the system integrates Tobler’s Hiking Function calibrated for Martian gravity (0.38g) alongside a dynamic metabolic oxygen model. Oxygen consumption scales in real time from 72 L/h (1.2 L/min) on flat terrain up to 228 L/h (3.8 L/min) on steep ascents, triggering automated fatigue warnings and dynamic Point-of-No-Return alerts (with a mandatory 25% reserve margin).

3- Tools, Software & Hardware Concepts

• Frontend & 3D Engine: Built with React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, and Three.js (WebGL) for real-time 3D planetary rendering, paired with Chart.js for elevation cross-sections.

• Data & Validation: Validated using a 50-point georeferenced matrix (jezero_terrain_matrix.csv) modeled after real NASA orbital observations of Jezero Crater, verified via Vitest unit testing and deployed on Vercel.

• Helmet Hardware Concept: Designed around an electrostatic dust-repellent polycarbonate visor with UV shielding, internal optical HUD projection, and direct integration with the Portable Life Support System (PLSS) and Liquid Cooling Garment (LCG).

4- Creativity, Key Factors & Intended Impact

Our team prioritized the physical realities of Mars exploration: the up to 20-minute Earth-Mars communication delay, astronaut cognitive load, and abrasive Martian dust. By combining tactical local autonomy with strategic Earth planning, RED-ARES maximizes scientific return per EVA minute while ensuring astronaut survival.

5- Transparency Note on Super Intelligence (SI) Use

The core concept, system architecture, and ideation of RED-ARES were entirely conceived by our team. Super Intelligence tools were utilized strictly as technical assistants for information gathering, data interpretation (structuring a 50-point synthetic test dataset modeled after NASA HiRISE/CRISM parameters), generating supplementary visual concepts, and editing technical documentation. All UI/UX design, web application development, and algorithm implementation were executed by the team.
